title: Zero Copy Federation vs Reverse ETL for Real-Time Segmentation

steps.prompt: Marketing needs Snowflake behavioral scores in Salesforce for near-real-time segmentation. The lake holds 50TB of raw clickstream; leadership rejects duplicating it into Salesforce storage or paying continuous API ingest fees. Which architecture best satisfies freshness, cost, and Trust?

options.label: Scheduled reverse ETL copying 50TB into Custom Big Objects nightly
options.rationale: Physically replicating 50TB creates storage bloat, stale caches between sync windows, and ongoing ingest cost — the antipattern Data 360 Zero Copy is designed to eliminate.

options.label: Data 360 inbound Zero Copy federation to Snowflake, exposing governed shares as Data Lake / Data Model Objects without moving the lake
options.rationale: Inbound Zero Copy federation lets Data 360 query Snowflake in place via governed shares, preserving freshness and avoiding lake duplication while still powering segments and insights.

options.label: Synchronous External Services REST callout on every record page view to fetch scores live
options.rationale: Per-view synchronous callouts degrade UI latency and burn callout rate limits; they do not provide a governed, queryable customer data layer for segmentation at scale.

title: DLO to DMO: Canonical Modeling Before Unification

steps.prompt: An ERP connector will land millions of order rows into Data 360. Architects must preserve source fidelity for reprocessing while still exposing a canonical Party/Engagement model for identity resolution and insights. What is the required modeling sequence?

options.label: Land raw rows in a Data Lake Object (DLO), then map DLO fields into standard or harmonized Data Model Objects (DMOs)
options.rationale: Data 360 separates immutable raw ingestion (DLO) from business semantics (DMO). Harmonizing after the lake layer keeps reprocessing possible and feeds identity resolution and calculated insights correctly.

options.label: Write ERP payloads straight into the Unified Individual DMO, skipping raw staging
options.rationale: Unified Individuals are outputs of identity resolution over mapped DMOs — not a direct ingest target. Skipping DLOs blocks reprocessing and breaks governed lineage.

options.label: Base64-encode every field into a single opaque DLO column to "secure" the feed
options.rationale: Opaque encoding destroys field-level mapping, segmentation filters, and insight engines. Trust is enforced with governance and encryption controls, not by making data unqueryable.

steps.prompt: A Data 360 Identity Resolution ruleset uses fuzzy match on Normalized Phone Number alone. Household members sharing a landline collapse into one Unified Individual, polluting consent and personalization. How should the ruleset be revised?

options.label: Require composite match criteria — e.g. phone plus exact First Name or Date of Birth — and keep reconciliation rules separate from match rules
options.rationale: Single-attribute fuzzy matching on shared identifiers causes Fuzzy Over-Clustering. Well-Architected rulesets combine high-signal attributes and treat reconciliation (field winners) as a separate stage after match groups form.

options.label: Disable Identity Resolution and unify profiles with custom Apex triggers on Contact
options.rationale: Identity Resolution is a distributed big-data graph process. Apex cannot reconcile millions of cross-source identities with the same scale, lineage, or governance.

options.label: Change only the reconciliation rule to "Most Recently Updated" and leave the phone-only match intact
options.rationale: Reconciliation chooses winning attribute values after records are already merged. It cannot undo over-merging caused by weak match criteria.

title: Lakehouse Zero Copy: Iceberg Federation vs Bulk JDBC Copy

steps.prompt: A company keeps 100TB of telemetry in Databricks as Apache Iceberg tables (Parquet). Product wants Data 360 insights on that telemetry without paying to duplicate the lake into Salesforce storage. Which approach is Well-Architected?

options.label: File-based Zero Copy federation via Iceberg REST Catalog metadata so Data 360 queries Parquet/Iceberg in place
options.rationale: Data 360 file federation for lakehouses relies on Apache Iceberg tabular metadata and Parquet files exposed through an Iceberg REST Catalog — enabling governed zero-copy access without moving 100TB.

options.label: Nightly JDBC extract that copies all 100TB into Data 360 DLOs for "local performance"
options.rationale: Bulk-copying a 100TB lake defeats Zero Copy economics: it multiplies storage cost, extends ingest windows, and creates freshness lag versus federated query.

options.label: Hourly SFTP drops of CSV extracts into a ContentVersion staging object
options.rationale: CSV/SFTP polling lacks lakehouse metadata federation, is high-latency, and is a poor fit for analytical telemetry at this scale.

title: Streaming vs Calculated Insights for Sub-Minute Triggers

steps.prompt: Commerce wants an engagement the moment a shopper views 3 products inside a 5-minute sliding window. Leadership will not accept next-day batch scores for this use case. Which Data 360 capability fits?

options.label: Streaming Insights with time-based sliding window aggregations over the browse event stream
options.rationale: Streaming Insights evaluate aggregations as events arrive, enabling near-real-time windowed triggers that batch Calculated Insights cannot meet.

options.label: Batch Calculated Insights scheduled once every 24 hours on historical browse history
options.rationale: Calculated Insights excel at scheduled historical metrics; a once-daily batch misses the live 5-minute browse window entirely.

options.label: Scheduled Apex Batch counting Product_View__c rows with SOQL
options.rationale: Apex/SOQL on CRM objects cannot economically process web-scale streaming telemetry or Data 360 streaming engines.

title: Data Actions: Bridging Insights to CRM Execution

steps.prompt: A Streaming Insight flags VIP churn risk above 85%. Retention must start in core CRM within minutes — without a custom polling service. How should Data 360 invoke the downstream workflow?

options.label: Configure a Data Action that publishes a Platform Event or invokes a Salesforce Flow when the insight threshold is met
options.rationale: Data Actions are the governed bridge from Data 360 insights to CRM execution (events, flows, and related targets), avoiding custom pollers while keeping the path declarative and observable.

options.label: Nightly Apex job that pages the Data 360 Query API looking for high-risk VIPs
options.rationale: Polling introduces multi-hour lag, wastes API/credit budget, and recreates integration debt that Data Actions already solve.

options.label: External Python daemon updating Contacts over the SOAP API whenever it scrapes insight exports
options.rationale: Unmanaged external daemons add operational debt, weaken Trust/auditability, and bypass native activation paths.

title: Unstructured Grounding: Chunking Knowledge in Data 360

steps.prompt: An Agentforce service agent must be grounded on 10,000 PDF manuals stored and indexed through Data 360 unstructured / search capabilities. Retrieval quality is poor and token spend is high. Which chunking strategy best balances semantic coherence with retrieval cost?

options.label: Semantic section-aware chunks (~250–500 tokens) with modest overlap and preserved heading metadata for retrieval filters
options.rationale: Moderate, structure-aware chunks keep procedures intact for embedding similarity while staying small enough for precise retrieval and controlled context-window cost when grounding agents from Data 360.

options.label: Embed each entire 50-page PDF as one vector so "nothing is lost"
options.rationale: Whole-document embeddings dilute local semantics, hurt cosine retrieval of specific procedures, and pull oversized context into the LLM — raising cost and hallucination risk.

options.label: Split every 10 characters regardless of word or section boundaries
options.rationale: Arbitrary micro-splits destroy lexical meaning and produce unusable retrieval units.

title: Segment Activation: Cloud Storage Egress at Audience Scale

steps.prompt: Marketing activates a 20-million-profile segment to Amazon S3 every morning for ad platforms. The design must avoid CRM API ceilings and keep egress operationally simple. Which activation pattern fits?

options.label: Data 360 cloud storage activation target exporting compressed Parquet/CSV directly to the S3 bucket
options.rationale: Cloud storage activation is built for high-volume parallel object egress to destinations like S3, avoiding per-row CRM API paths while keeping the activation governed inside Data 360.

options.label: Apex trigger issuing millions of individual S3 REST callouts as Contacts update
options.rationale: Synchronous/near-synchronous Apex callouts cannot egress 20M profiles without exhausting API, CPU, and callout governors.

options.label: Export the full audience as a CSV email attachment to the campaign ops alias
options.rationale: Email attachments hit size limits and create uncontrolled PII copies outside governed activation channels — a Trust and Reliability failure.

title: Data Subject Erasure Across Data 360 Lake and Unified Profiles

steps.prompt: A customer submits a GDPR Right to Erasure request. Records exist in source CRM, Data 360 DLOs, unified DMOs, and derived insights. What must the architect ensure for complete compliance?

options.label: Execute a governed Data Subject Rights / Forget Me request in Data 360 so erasure propagates across lake objects, unified profiles, and derived insights — coordinated with source-system deletion
options.rationale: Data 360 retains historical lake and unified layers independently of CRM deletes. A formal data subject request is required to purge or restrict processing across DLOs, DMOs, and derived artifacts while source systems handle their own copies.

options.label: Delete the Contact in core CRM and assume Data 360 will drop the profile on the next connector sync
options.rationale: Connector syncs do not automatically cryptographically erase historical lake snapshots and unified graphs. Relying on CRM delete alone leaves residual PII in Data 360.

options.label: Rename the Contact to "Deleted User" in the CRM UI and leave lake objects untouched
options.rationale: Cosmetic field edits leave PII in underlying lakehouse and insight layers, failing GDPR audit requirements.

title: Credit Economics: Stop Streaming Static Catalog Feeds

steps.prompt: Data 360 credits are burning down early each month. An audit finds 50 streaming connectors on product catalog tables that change about once a week, while scarce credit headroom is needed for real-time behavioral streams. What refactor is required?

options.label: Move slow-changing catalog ingestion from continuous streaming connectors to scheduled batch ingestion
options.rationale: Streaming Everything on near-static sources wastes continuous compute credits. Batch ingestion matches catalog change cadence and reserves streaming budget for true real-time signals.

options.label: Buy 10× more credits and leave the streaming topology unchanged
options.rationale: Purchasing capacity without fixing waste violates Cost Optimization and merely delays the next credit cliff.

options.label: Disable encryption on catalog objects to reduce compute cost
options.rationale: Weakening encryption to save credits destroys Trust and compliance boundaries; credit governance must not sacrifice security controls.

title: ETL storage hoarding to Zero-Copy: 4-stage Data Virtualization refactor

stages.scenario: An enterprise replicates 50 million legacy ERP billing and invoice line records into custom sObjects via hourly scheduled ETL batch pipelines. The org has exceeded its licensed Salesforce data storage by 140%, resulting in heavy monthly storage overage penalties. Furthermore, batch API jobs frequently fail during peak hours due to 24-hour API limit exhaustion, leaving sales reps with out-of-sync invoice records. What is the fundamental architectural antipattern?

options.text: The architecture commits 'ETL Data Hoarding': replicating cold, read-mostly reference data into transactional Salesforce storage instead of querying it at source on demand via Data Virtualization.
options.coachingFeedback: Correct! The Salesforce Data Virtualization guide emphasizes that high-volume, read-mostly operational data should not be physically replicated into transactional relational storage, which wastes storage credits and consumes API limits.

options.text: The custom sObject should be converted into Big Objects to completely eliminate all API usage.
options.coachingFeedback: Misconception: Ingesting data into Big Objects still requires API calls and Async SOQL for complex querying; it does not eliminate ETL pipeline maintenance.

options.text: Hourly ETL pipelines are required by Salesforce for any external system containing more than 1 million records.
options.coachingFeedback: False: Salesforce encourages Zero Copy patterns and Data Virtualization via Salesforce Connect and Data 360 to eliminate unnecessary ETL pipelines.

stages.scenario: To eliminate physical storage overhead while providing seamless real-time access to ERP invoices directly on Account page layouts, what target pattern does the Data Virtualization fundamentals guide recommend?

options.text: Deploy Salesforce Connect with External Objects mapped to the data source (OData or Snowflake), configuring Query Pushdown, Indirect Lookups to Account, and dual governance through Named/Per-User Principals.
options.coachingFeedback: Correct! According to the Data Virtualization guide, Salesforce Connect with External Objects leverages Query Pushdown to execute filtering at source, renders external data seamlessly in standard UI components, and consumes zero Salesforce relational storage.

options.text: Build a custom Lightning Web Component that executes synchronous Apex HTTP REST callouts to the ERP system on every page load.
options.coachingFeedback: Antipattern: Ad-hoc Apex callouts in UI components lack native declarative integration (reports, Flow lookups, list views), risk thread exhaustion, and fail to leverage platform query pushdown optimizations.

stages.scenario: How should the enterprise safely transition users from the legacy custom sObject to External Objects without disrupting daily sales operations?

options.text: Deploy External Objects side-by-side on a dedicated Lightning page tab for a pilot user group, validate source query latency and Indirect Lookup indexing, and then decommission the hourly ETL jobs followed by staged truncation of the legacy custom object records.
options.coachingFeedback: Correct! Well-Architected migration prescribes side-by-side pilot validation to verify source query pushdown responsiveness before shutting down ETL replication and reclaiming physical storage.

options.text: Immediately delete all 50 million custom object records with Bulk API Hard Delete before setting up the External Data Source.
options.coachingFeedback: Catastrophic risk: Deleting legacy data before external connectivity and lookups are validated creates severe business downtime if the external connection fails.

stages.scenario: What observability mechanism should be implemented to ensure the virtualized data layer maintains high availability and stays within external callout constraints?

options.text: Monitor External Data Callout metrics via Event Monitoring, track OData response times and HTTP 429/500 status codes, and set automated alerts on named credential authentication expiration.
options.coachingFeedback: Correct! Real-time telemetry on External Data Callouts ensures architects can monitor source query latencies, detect external rate limits, and proactively refresh credentials before user sessions fail.

options.text: Assume the external system is always healthy since External Objects do not consume standard SOQL query rows.
options.coachingFeedback: Antipattern: External systems can suffer outages, latency degradation, or credential rotations that break the virtualized UI if unmonitored.
